Features

A CAD preprocessor, viewer, hierarchy editor and exporter in one local app.

In motion

Four tools at work.

STEP to GLB

Convert

  • Reads the whole assemblyColours, names and the full part tree come straight out of OpenCascade.
  • Finds repeatsThe same shape at any angle or position becomes one mesh drawn many times.
  • Rebuilds the surfacesSet the detail in millimetres or as a share of the model’s size, and let it drop what’s too small to matter.
  • CompressesMeshopt, through gltfpack, makes GLBs about ten times smaller.
  • Reads IGES and BREP tooThe converter and the upload take .iges, .igs, .brep and .brp as well as STEP. IGES keeps the names, colours and layers the file has.
  • A whole folder at once--batch converts every CAD file in a folder, one process each so a damaged file can’t stop the run, and writes a table of what happened.
  • Level-of-detail files--lod 100,50,25 writes the same model three times, lighter each time, with the same nodes, names and instances.
  • Keeps what the CAD file knewEach node carries its name in the CAD tree, its assembly path, part number, colour, layers and volume, wherever the file has them.
  • One click to startstart.bat or start.command sets up Python and opens the browser.
  • Long jobs in the backgroundA big conversion runs as a job and its progress shows in the window.

Features

Look around

  • WebGPU, with WebGL2 as a fallbackThe renderer can be switched in Settings.
  • Real lightingA studio to reflect, soft shadows in the corners, fog on the floor.
  • Dark parts you can still readA studio to reflect on plain backgrounds and a headlight that follows the view, so black parts keep an edge and a sheen.
  • Click what you seeHover, click and box-select work on the parts you see, copies included.
  • Hide, isolate, soloOne key each, to cut the noise and focus.
  • RecolourBy group, by material or per part, with a reset.
  • Five ways to see itSolid, wireframe, x-ray, heatmap and clay. Clay shows every part in one plain material; right-click it for porcelain, steel or red wax.

Features

Clean up

  • Smart optimiseRuns every clean-up in one go and undoes in one step.
  • FastenersFinds bolts, screws, nuts and washers by their shape and selects them.
  • Select hidden partsPicks the parts that can’t be seen from outside, ready to delete.
  • Stacked copiesFinds parts drawn twice in the same place and keeps one. It only removes a part when an identical one sits in the same place, so 400 placed bolts stay 400.
  • Finds copies in other tools’ filesA GLB, FBX, OBJ or 3MF that writes the same bolt out again for every place it is used is searched for repeats when it opens. A 600-mesh test file went from 2.72 MB to 186 KB.
  • Decimate within a distanceType a number of millimetres and triangles go for as long as no point of the surface moves further than that. The result is measured, not trusted.
  • RecipesSmart optimise saves its settings under a name and runs them again later, or hands them to someone as a small file.
  • Merge by colourOne mesh per colour for the selection or for everything you can see. One undo.
  • Fill holesCloses bolt holes, slots and pockets in flat faces and leaves the rest. You can set the size, the depth and which kinds of hole.
  • DecimateReduces the selection by a percentage or to a triangle count, and keeps normals, UVs and vertex colours.
  • SplitBrings back the separate solids of a mesh that was fused on export.
  • Smart fitSwaps a part for a simple stand-in: a box, a turned box, a cylinder, a few boxes, or blocks that keep the outline.
  • Fit to budgetGive it a triangle count for the whole scene and it reduces the heaviest meshes first, with a preview.
  • Align to floorStands a model that arrived on its side on the grid.
  • Delete small partsRemoves parts too small to see, plus empty, duplicate and broken ones.
  • What it savedEvery action shows the triangles it removed, and every part remembers what it arrived with.

Features

The part tree

  • Built for big assembliesTen thousand rows scroll smoothly, because only the rows you can see are drawn.
  • Search and filtersFind parts by name, and tint the small ones.
  • Flatten, dissolve, ungroupCollapse chains of single groups, dissolve a group, or ungroup a branch.
  • Batch rename (F2)Templates, find and replace with regular expressions, and presets.
  • Organise from the right-click menuTake a group out and keep what was in it, flatten a group, sort inside it A to Z or Z to A, move it up or down, delete the empty ones, open or close a whole branch.
  • Groups and parts togetherCtrl toggles a row as a unit, Shift picks the range from the last row you clicked, groups and parts alike.
  • Undo and redoTree edits, recolouring, renames and clean-ups share one history.
  • Right-click menuHide, isolate, recolour, rename or frame a part from one menu.

Lines are parts

Draw and sweep

  • A Draw tool (L)Pen, rectangle, circle, arc, polygon, freehand and edit, on the ground, the front, the side, the view or the face of a part.
  • Dots you can snap toA field of dots follows the grid near the pointer and a click a few pixels off still lands on a dot. Handles snap too.
  • Edit any lineDrag points and handles, click a curve to add a point, double-click for smooth or sharp. Ctrl-drag breaks a handle from its partner.
  • Round or cut the cornersDrag the ring on the corner of a rectangle or polygon and every corner follows. Round or Bevel is one click.
  • A line is a row in the treeRename it, hide it, group it, nest it, move it with the gizmo. One undo for everything.
  • Properties like Cinema 4DA Shape card for width, radius, sides and corners, and a Spline card with Type, Close and Interpolation: None, Natural, Uniform, Adaptive or Subdivided.
  • SweepCarry a circle, a rectangle or another line along a path, with scale at both ends, a twist and closed ends. The result is a normal part.

Features

Build

  • A library of 86 partsBolts, nuts, pipe fittings, profiles, gears and a stepper motor. Look at one, change its size, then drag it in.
  • A bolt with its own nutThe nut is part of the bolt, so it moves and undoes with it.
  • Exploded viewPull the parts apart with a slider for each axis.
  • MeasureClick two points. The measurements stay in a list and can be picked again.

Features

Export

  • GLB and glTFWith Draco or Meshopt compression, and textures embedded if you want them.
  • FBX, USDZ, OBJ, STL, PLYCommon 3D and AR formats, with scale presets for mm, cm, m and inches.
  • Parts listA CSV bill of materials: every part and its size.
  • Check against where it’s goingCompare the scene with the published guidance for a web page, a Shopify product, Apple AR Quick Look or a phone app, before and after exporting.
  • Save sceneKeeps the view, the selection and the recolouring in a small file next to the model.

Features

The app

  • Start screenDrop a file anywhere, open a recent one, or begin from a shape.
  • Scene tabsEach tab is its own scene. Opening a file never replaces one that has something in it.
  • Cards beside the modelA tool with settings opens as a card. Enter runs it and Esc puts it away.
  • Numbers you dragDrag any number sideways to change it, or click to type.
  • One Settings windowGeneral, viewport, camera, performance, scene and storage, with one search for all of it.
  • Search (Ctrl or ⌘ + K)Every command, every part in the scene and every part in the library.
  • ShortcutsA searchable list of every key.
  • Comes back where you left itYour files and saved scenes are still there after a reload.
  • Looks after itselfThe server closes with the window, a crash is noticed at the next start and offers Reopen and Safe mode, and a warning shows when the graphics card is not in use.
  • Non-destructiveThe original geometry isn’t touched until you export.
  • No build stepPlain JavaScript and CSS. Edit a file, refresh, done.

A closer look

The details, in pictures.

All screenshots
01

One button, half the triangles

Smart optimise runs every clean-up the app has, in order: empty and broken parts, hidden parts, fasteners, tiny parts, holes in flat faces, and then a reduction to the target you set. On this derailleur it took 1,103,373 triangles down to 552,115 and showed what it had saved. One Ctrl+Z puts it all back.

02

Bolts, found by their shape

Names in a CAD export rarely say what a part is. Fasteners cuts each part across its axis and reads the outline: a round shank with a wider head, six flats around a hole, a flat ring. It finds hex bolts, socket screws, nuts and washers whatever they’re called, and leaves bushings, bearings and O-rings alone. Twelve here, 129,460 triangles.

03

172,894 triangles down to 114

Smart fit used to turn a bracket into a brick. Blocks rebuilds a part from a coarse grid, so its steps, arms and openings stay where they were. Here it took the two heaviest parts of the derailleur from 172,894 triangles to 114.

04

A bolt that brings its own nut

Tick it on, pick the nut and set how far from the head it sits. The nut is part of the bolt’s own shape, in the bolt’s thread. It’s one part in the tree and one undo step, and it can’t slide off the end.

05

Pull it apart

The exploded view has a slider for each axis, so you can open a gearbox along one direction only. Put it back with one click on the pill next to the camera.

06

Tabs you can arrange

Every tab is a scene of its own, with its own undo history. Drag them into order, save from the tab’s icon, and your sidebars stay where you put them from one scene to the next.

07

It starts like an app

Installed, it opens in a window of its own with no address bar and no browser tabs. Drop a STEP, GLB, glTF, FBX, OBJ, 3MF or STL file anywhere on the start screen, or begin from a shape.

Run it on your own machine.

Free and open source under the MIT licence. Windows and macOS; your files never leave the computer.
